subject: Mechanical Engineering
title: Shear: Sliding Sideways
description: A quick, practical guide to Shear: Sliding Sideways.

hook.text: Scissors cut paper by pushing two blades past each other. That sliding force is shear — layers moving in opposite directions.

buildup.text: A bolt holding two plates together feels shear stress. The plates try to slide, and the bolt resists across its cross section.

discovery.text: Shear strain is the angle of deformation — how much a square tilts into a parallelogram under sideways force.

twist.text: Most materials are weaker in shear than in tension. A shaft twists and fails in shear long before it pulls apart.

climax.text: Rivets, welds, and adhesive joints all carry shear loads. Designing for shear is crucial in every bolted connection.

punchline.text: Tension pulls. Compression pushes. Shear slides. Three forces, three limits.

quiz.question: How does shear stress act on a bolt connecting two plates?
options: It pulls the bolt lengthwise, stretching it like a spring
It pushes the bolt straight down into the lower plate
It slides the plates in opposite directions across the bolt's cross section
